title: observability: token-level KV metrics + tracing dashboard and alert tuning
author: Aisha Kumar
description: Context: We have recurring incidents where KV cache inefficiencies cause unexpected token-level cost spikes and increased tail latency for small requests. ENG-1245 asked for token-level KV metrics and tracing to make root-cause analysis tractable and to drive tighter alert conditions. Motivation: Add finer-grained metrics (KV hit/miss per-token, prefix cache reuse ratios), correlate KV behavior with token-level latency and cost, provide a combined dashboard for SRE and runtime teams, and tune alerts to reduce noisy paging while catching regressions quickly. What this PR does: 1) Introduces new Prometheus metrics: redwood_kv_token_hits_total, redwood_kv_token_misses_total, redwood_kv_cache_prefix_reuse_ratio, redwood_token_service_duration_seconds_bucket (kv-scoped label), and redwood_token_cost_estimate_cents_total. 2) Adds trace spans around KV lookup/insert paths and attaches token-level metadata (request_id, model, seq_len_bucket). 3) Implements a Grafana dashboard (observability/token_kv_token_level) that shows per-model token hit/miss rates, KV latency distribution, token-level cost breakdown and correlated trace links. 4) Tunes alert rules: reduces false positives by switching from absolute thresholds to anomaly-rate-of-change plus SLO-aware thresholds; adds a 5-minute suppression window for known warmup patterns. 5) Updates docs and runbooks with debugging steps and alert playbook. Implementation notes: - Metrics exposed from runtime's kv_cache module (kv_cache/metrics.rs and runtime/observability.rs). Metrics use existing redwood_prom exporter naming and follow cardinality limits by bucketizing sequence length and model_family labels. - Tracing uses opentelemetry with a lightweight token-level span emitted only on miss path or when latency > p95 to avoid high cardinality. - Dashboard panels are grouped: Overview (cost & latency), KV health (hit/miss, reuse), Tracing samples (links to jaeger), and Alerts (recent fires + suggested action). - Alerts use a composite rule: (relative increase in miss-rate over rolling baseline) AND (miss-rate above model-specific threshold) to avoid alerts during deployments. Testing: - Unit tests for metrics registration and label cardinality checks added. - Synthetic load tests run in perf-canary: compared baseline to new metrics and verified no measurable CPU overhead (<0.5%). - End-to-end tracing validated on staging with sample traces linked from dashboard. Rollout plan: - Feature gated behind runtime flag obs_token_kv_metrics (off by default). - Enable in dedicated staging first for two weeks, then ramp to hosted on low-traffic region, monitor for noise. Docs & runbooks: - Added docs/observability/token_kv_playbook.md and updated runbooks/incident_kv_cache.md. Follow-ups: - ENG-1302 follow-up to add automated remediation (fallback to bypass KV for high-miss models). - Consider adding delta-cost alerts per-customer in a future PR. Checklist: - [x] Metrics exported and unit-tested - [x] Tracing spans added with sampling guard - [x] Grafana dashboard JSON checked in - [x] Alert rules adjusted and sim-tested - [x] Runbooks and docs updated

review_comments: Jonah Lee: Nice work — can you explain cardinality controls for model label? Concern about adding per-model high-cardinality labels.
Aisha Kumar: We bucket by model_family and sequence_length (seq_len_bucket) and limit model label to top-10 models via a runtime whitelist. Added unit tests to validate label cardinality.
Marta Gonzales: Alert composite rule looks good; suggest adding a decay window to avoid flapping during rollouts.
Aisha Kumar: Added 10-minute decaying baseline and 5-minute suppression for deployment signals. Also added notes in runbook.
Priya Reddy: Verified Grafana JSON — panels render correctly in staging. One nit: move KV latency histogram next to cost breakdown for easier correlation.
Aisha Kumar: Moved panel as requested and added a link to jaeger traces for sampled spans.
